newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS SIGN QB FREROTTE TO FOUR-YEAR, $18 MILLION DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS SIGN QB FREROTTE TO FOUR-YEAR, $18 MILLION DEAL.

text.p: The Washington Redskins signed quarterback Gus Frerotte to a four-year contract on Friday worth $18 million.

The deal, which includes a signing bonus of $5 million, was announced five days after Frerotte accepted a one-year offer worth $1.04 million when talks for a long-term contract failed to produce an agreement.

"There is no question that this is best for Gus and the Washington Redskins," said coach Norv Turner. "He has worked hard over the course of his entire career to reach this point. The long-term contract will add to the stability of the team."
Frerotte accepted a one-year offer from the team on Sunday in order to attend camp early in the week, but he and the team continued to negotiate to hammer out a multi-year agreement.
Frerotte will earn a cap-friendly base salary of $750,000 in 1997. The yearly salaries then escalate to $1.95 million in 1998, $4.5 million in 1999 and $5.8 million in 2000.

A seventh-round pick from Tulsa in 1994, Frerotte won the starting job from Heath Shuler in last year's training camp battle and was named to the Pro Bowl. He led the Redskins to a 7-1 record in the first half of the season, but Washington struggled to a 2-6 mark in the second half and barely missed the playoffs with a 9-7 record.
Frerotte passed for 3,453 yards last season, second only to Brett Favre in the NFC, with 12 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.

The Redskins signed veteran Jeff Hostetler last month to serve as a backup to Frerotte. Hostetler completed 60 percent of his passes for 2,548 yards with 23 touchdowns and 14 interceptions in 13 games last season with the Raiders.
